notes: A running account of where things stand by these headlines, revised after each edition rather than added to. Every version is kept.
Written by the model from the narratives, not from the headlines. It is a reading, not a record.
standing: By these headlines the Iran war's fuel squeeze has moved from the petrol pump to products refined from oil: US airlines are charging about 23% more after jet fuel rose more than 90%, an easyJet flight left Naples for Berlin without luggage, Estonia ran out of asphalt, and Malaysia, India, Ukraine and South Korea are changing fuel and power rules. Lula has won Brazil's run-off after Donald Trump called the vote rigged, and Flávio Bolsonaro is reported travelling to the United States with talk of asylum, while about 300 US soldiers have arrived in Colombia and Corina Machado has returned to Venezuela. Anthropic has filed for a record US share listing and is being sued by Elvis Presley's rights holders over 200 songs. Students were reported on strike or occupying buildings in France, Mexico, India and Italy, and public schemes in six countries, from Canadian surgery to German care bills and Lucknow pharmacies, are reported as falling short and passing costs to households.
moved: The Iran and fuel thread moved from talks and strike preparation on 26 October, to US petrol and European gas prices on the morning of 27 October, to jet fuel, bitumen and state pricing rules by that evening.

The Brazil thread moved from how Brazil's vote was read abroad, to Trump calling it rigged, to the United States as a destination for the defeated right and a military presence in Colombia after Lula's win.
Three threads began on the evening of 27 October: public schemes falling short, AI-made faces and files in checks built for people, and broadcasts removed over offence.
silent: Drones as one machine doing many jobs, the night the world watched one football match, and courts re-sentencing past events have had no narrative since 26 October. The first editions were written in a looser, more figurative style than the later ones, so this is at least partly a change in the collection's manner rather than the world moving on.

threads.label: Iran war, Hormuz and fuel
threads.text: On 26 October the join was the Gulf running talks and strike preparations side by side. On the morning of 27 October it was the Hormuz oil shock raising US petrol and European gas prices while Iran hosted Gulf security talks. By the evening of 27 October it had reached products refined from oil and the rules that price them: Fortune reported US airlines charging about 23% more for emptier planes after jet fuel rose more than 90%, an easyJet flight left Naples for Berlin without luggage, Estonia ran out of asphalt, and Malaysia, India, Ukraine and South Korea were adjusting fuel formulas, blending caps, power incentives and reactor licences. The easyJet and Estonia reports do not themselves name the war.
threads.direction: It has moved from diplomacy and strike preparation to the pump and then to jet fuel, bitumen and state pricing rules.

threads.label: Brazil's election and the United States
threads.text: On 26 October the join was Brazil's vote being read as a script in Buenos Aires, Madrid and Nairobi. On the morning of 27 October it narrowed to Donald Trump calling the Brazilian election rigged while offering $1 million for evidence of fraud in US elections. By the evening of 27 October, after Lula's run-off win, the United States appeared as the common party: Flávio Bolsonaro reported travelling there with talk of asylum, Lula warning of persecution and foreign money, about 300 US soldiers arriving in Colombia for anti-drug exercises, and Machado's return to Venezuela read as a test of US influence. The asylum report rests on allies and unnamed sources.
threads.direction: It has moved from how Brazil's vote is read abroad to Washington's part in what follows the result.

threads.label: AI companies' listing, land and lawsuits
threads.text: On 26 October the join was an AI company listing the end of the world as a risk factor in its prospectus and the market buying the shares. Early on 27 October an edition followed data centres down to county level, where requests for land, grid connections and water were being refused. On the morning of 27 October Anthropic filed for a record US share listing as Elvis Presley's rights holders sued it over 200 songs. This thread was formed in this first Chronicle by joining the listing narratives with the county data-centre narrative, which did not name Anthropic. It had no narrative on the evening of 27 October.
threads.direction: It has moved from the prospectus to the ground and to the courts, and was not touched in the latest edition.

threads.label: Students striking and occupying
threads.text: On 26 October the join was young people in public squares: students had brought down a government, and a president was copying a teenage dance. On the morning of 27 October it became concrete and spread across countries, with students on strike or occupying buildings in France, Mexico, India and Italy, Serbia expected next, and police action at universities in the frame. It had no narrative on the evening of 27 October, so whether the strikes grew or ended is not shown by these headlines.
threads.direction: It moved from youth as a political image to named strikes and occupations, then went unmentioned in the latest edition.

threads.label: Money leaving and states offering discounts
threads.text: Early on 27 October one narrative joined savings and fortunes moving into dollars, gold and trusts with states answering by amnesties and discounts meant to bring the money back into view. No narrative in the two editions since has followed it. It stands as a single observation rather than a run across editions, and by these headlines the question of capital leaving and of tax amnesties to recover it has not returned since that edition.

threads.label: AI buyouts and dangerous manual work
threads.text: Early on 27 October one narrative set office workers being paid to leave as AI takes their tasks against labourers still dying in ditches, fields and collapsed buildings. The join was a split in how work ends: a buyout for the clerk and an accident for the manual worker. No later narrative has carried it, though AI appeared again on the evening of 27 October in a different join about fakes in checks built for people.

threads.label: Rites counted before the days of the dead
threads.text: Early on 27 October one narrative joined reports that measured the rites of late October and early November before they happen: numbers of hosts, incense sticks, costumes and the strain on worshippers' knees. It was a seasonal join and no narrative has carried it since. With the days of the dead still ahead, it may return in later editions, but by these headlines nothing has yet followed it.

threads.label: European household readiness and borrowed deterrence
threads.text: Early on 27 October one narrative joined European advice that households should be able to last 72 hours on their own with European states seeking cover from nuclear warheads they do not themselves own. The join placed civil preparation at the kitchen-cupboard level beside talk of extended deterrence between states. No narrative in the two editions since has returned to it, so it stands as a single observation.

threads.label: State housing drives and housing protests
threads.text: On the morning of 27 October one narrative joined Egypt, Indonesia and Tamil Nadu expanding housing through states and employers with Portugal investigating police conduct at housing protests, and the part property funds play. It set state building programmes beside street protest over the cost of a home. No narrative followed it on the evening of 27 October, though that edition's thread on public schemes falling short touches a nearby question of who pays.

threads.label: Public schemes passing costs to households
threads.text: Begun on the evening of 27 October. In six countries a public scheme meant to cover a cost was reported as falling short: Canadians paying for private surgery from savings and GoFundMe, German adult children billed for parents' care, Lucknow's subsidised generic pharmacies short of medicines, a Bangladeshi antivenom programme lacking funds, compensation claims from 50,000 Australians over unlawful Centrelink suspensions, and doubt over a Mexican voluntary pension scheme. The case against notes that several of these stories have run for years and one is a wealth-advice column, so no widening of the gaps is yet shown.

threads.label: AI-made faces and files in checks
threads.text: Begun on the evening of 27 October. Nigeria's electoral commission is investigating suspected AI-generated photos in the voters' register, New Zealand job seekers report being ignored as AI-written applications flood employers, an Australian court passed the first sentence under deepfake laws without jail, and fashion models face AI copies of their image. The join is that a plausible picture or document now costs little to make while checking it still takes a person's time. Several cited cases, in Japan, the Philippines and Ghana, use methods older than generative software.

threads.label: Broadcasts and films removed over offence
threads.text: Begun on the evening of 27 October. A Chinese platform dropped Racing-Real Madrid and La Liga broadcasts were suspended after a remark by Mbappé, an Indian court ordered a documentary on Adani and Modi taken down, a Korean drama faced calls to halt over a Gwangju episode, and Neil Young sued to stop Trump rallies using his songs, while police in Jordan, Egypt and Spain acted against content and a Mexican court struck down a state propaganda law. Three of the headlines are the same Mbappé story from different countries.

threads.label: Drones doing many civil and military jobs
threads.text: On 26 October one narrative joined drones cutting power, guarding a lake, carrying the wounded and being sold, treating one kind of machine as the common object across war, policing, rescue and trade. No narrative has carried it in the three editions since.

threads.label: One football night watched worldwide
threads.text: On 26 October one narrative joined coverage of a single football night that drew attention across many countries at once. It was tied to one event and no narrative has carried it since. Football returned on 27 October only as a broadcasting dispute in the removal-over-offence thread.

threads.label: Courts re-sentencing past events
threads.text: On 26 October one narrative joined courts re-sentencing events of 1979 and 1996 with a library removing material from 2026, treating them as revisions of the record. No narrative has carried it in the three editions since, though the Korean drama over Gwangju on 27 October touches the same ground.

caseAgainst: This first Chronicle rests on four editions published within about 21 hours, so it cannot yet speak of weeks or even several days. None of the narratives carried a formal continuation link; the runs in the fuel, Brazil, AI industry and student threads are my grouping, supported in two cases by the narratives' own reference to the previous edition, and the brief that asks for continuity may have encouraged both the writers and me to see it. The first two editions were written in a looser, figurative style and the later ones in a literal style, which makes matching across them a matter of judgement, and that change of style may explain why some threads look silent. The AI industry thread was merged to keep within twelve live threads, and a reader could fairly split it. The sample leans on US business outlets such as Fortune and CNBC, many Brazilian outlets and many Spanish-language sports outlets, which enlarges the US view of the fuel shock, the Bolsonaro departures and the La Liga dispute. Today's two lead narratives also have weak links of their own: the easyJet and Estonia items do not name the Iran war, and the Bolsonaro asylum story rests on allies and unnamed sources.
revision: This is the first version of the Chronicle. It sets out seventeen threads, fourteen live and three silent, after joining the AI listing narratives with the county data-centre narrative into one thread, which leaves thirteen live; to stay within twelve live threads a further merge would be needed, and the single-observation threads begun on the early 27 October edition will turn silent first.
